item.title: Off the grid: explorer Ed Stafford & JETOUR test off-road boundaries in Harbin
item.dc:creator: TechNode Staff
item.description: Editor’s note: sponsored post In an event blending intelligent automotive engineering with the ethos of wilderness exploration, JETOUR hosted some of the brand friends for an interesting conversation with world-renowned explorer Ed Stafford, off-road demonstration, and official vehicle handover ceremony in Harbin, China. Joined by senior executives—including Ke Chuandeng, President of JETOUR International, and Yan Jun, Executive Vice President […]
item.content:encoded:
Editor’s note: sponsored post

In an event blending intelligent automotive engineering with the ethos of wilderness exploration, JETOUR hosted some of the brand friends for an interesting conversation with world-renowned explorer Ed Stafford, off-road demonstration, and official vehicle handover ceremony in Harbin, China.

Joined by senior executives—including Ke Chuandeng, President of JETOUR International, and Yan Jun, Executive Vice President of JETOUR International—the event brought together brand friends to experience the capabilities of JETOUR’s latest off-road lineup firsthand.

Testing Boundaries: Off-Road Performance

The event kicked off at a campsite, where brand friends joined Stafford, Ke, and Yan for an interactive field dialogue. The discussion focused on the intersection of modern vehicle design, off-road capabilities, and survival skills.
Addressing why JETOUR selected Stafford—the first person to hike the entire length of the Amazon River and host of several Discovery Channel series—Ke emphasized alignment in core values.

“The G700 is more than just a vehicle; it represents the courage to explore and go further. When we thought about who truly embodies the spirit of the G700, Ed was among the first to come to mind,” Ke stated. “For decades, Ed has navigated rainforests, deserts, and remote terrains worldwide. That passion for extreme exploration is precisely the philosophy behind the G700.”

Ke revealed that Stafford decided to purchase a G700 after driving it during the filming of Adventure of Extremes.

Reflecting on his experiences with the vehicle across various international locations, Stafford noted the SUV’s versatile performance.

Stafford said he was impressed with the ability to go to different places, when asked about his experience with the G700.

“I was impressed with the car’s ability to go to different places. I’ve had it in the sand dunes, huge sand dunes in Morocco. I’ve been up sort of rainforest covered mountains in Ecuador. I have been in desert conditions again, but sort of flat arid deserts in Colombia. Where else? Iceland. Obviously, the extreme cold of Iceland, and the car’s been able to handle everything,” he said.

“That’s the main thing, and it ties in with the values and the spirit of exploration because it’s not just a car for one thing; it’s a car for all exploration to all different places. And I think, in terms of the brand collaboration, I’m very happy to partner with Jetour, not just because it’s an amazing car,” he said.

“I do obviously share this desire to help people access wild places, and I think it’s very wholesome for people to spend more time outdoors, less time glued to their phones, more time hiking in the mountains. It’s a good reset for everyone in a world where everyone is very occupied with social media,” he said.

Ke concurred and said, “Exactly! I have G700 with me now. Every weekend, I never stay in the house. I always take any opportunity to drive my car out of the city to find some place I’ve never visited to try the car, to refresh my mind.”

“But before that, before I have the G700, I just stay in the house. The G700 has brought me a new life,” he quipped.

Engineering for Extreme Conditions

During the conversation with brand friends, Yan also detailed the technical specifications and testing standards behind the G700 platform.
Positioned as a luxury hybrid off-road SUV, the G700 is built on JETOUR’s GAIA Architecture. Designed to balance off-road performance with passenger comfort, the vehicle comes equipped with three professional off-road differential locks as standard equipment to handle complex terrain.

Addressing the role of real-world testing in product development, Yan underscored JETOUR’s global validation process.

“Laboratory testing gives us baseline data, but real-world environments are where vehicles must prove their reliability,” Yan explained. “We have established a unified global testing system where our vehicles have completed over 10 million kilometers of validation across extreme heat, cold, humidity, and high altitudes. We also conduct localized testing in each target market prior to launch.”

Following the conversation at the campsite, brand friends were given opportunities in a test ride and drive session on off-road tracks to evaluate the G700’s handling and terrain management systems.

Showroom Walkthrough & Vehicle Handover

Later in the afternoon, guests were invited to the Harbin JETOUR Experience Center, where Li Xueyong, Executive Vice President of Chery Automobile. Co Ltd, met with Stafford for an exclusive tour of the facility.

The showroom featured key models from the brand’s portfolio, including the JETOUR G700, JETOUR F700, and the specialized JETOUR G700 Topfire edition. The day concluded with an official gift exchange and handover ceremony, during which Li formally presented Stafford with the keys to his new G700.

The five- and six-seat SUV was launched on Aug. 5, with promotional prices ranging from RMB201,800 to RMB223,800. The H10 uses GWM’s Hi4 plug-in hybrid system and a 42.8-kilowatt-hour battery, providing up […]
item.content:encoded:
Great Wall Motor’s Haval brand said its H10 boxy SUV received more than 31,826 orders during its first 24 hours on the market. The five- and six-seat SUV was launched on Aug. 5, with promotional prices ranging from RMB201,800 to RMB223,800.

The H10 uses GWM’s Hi4 plug-in hybrid system and a 42.8-kilowatt-hour battery, providing up to 232 kilometers of CLTC electric range and a claimed total range of 1,404 kilometers. The vehicle also comes with lidar and the company’s Coffee Pilot 3 driver-assistance system. [TechNode reporting]

item.title: BYD and Sinopec Convert Shanghai Gas Station into Fast-Charging Site
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: BYD and Sinopec have converted a Shanghai gas station into a BYD Flash Charging flagship station, ending the site’s fuel operations. The station, located at 1209 Huqingping Road, is now operated as a charging site, while Sinopec’s Easy Joy convenience store remains open. The conversion follows a cooperation framework signed by the two companies in […]
item.content:encoded:
BYD and Sinopec have converted a Shanghai gas station into a BYD Flash Charging flagship station, ending the site’s fuel operations. The station, located at 1209 Huqingping Road, is now operated as a charging site, while Sinopec’s Easy Joy convenience store remains open.

The conversion follows a cooperation framework signed by the two companies in June covering fast-charging networks, integrated services and supply-chain cooperation. The project marks the first visible rollout of their plan to combine charging infrastructure with Sinopec’s retail network. [BYD]

The scheduled-task feature can handle recurring work such as compiling industry news and sorting emails. The office assistant can connect to notes, calendars and email, operate browsers, process […]
item.content:encoded:
Alibaba’s Qwen app has added scheduled tasks, an office assistant, voice calls, a research mode and an agent marketplace, while adding support for the Qwen3.8-Max flagship model.

The scheduled-task feature can handle recurring work such as compiling industry news and sorting emails. The office assistant can connect to notes, calendars and email, operate browsers, process files and generate office documents. The app also supports cross-device workflows in which tasks started on a phone can be executed on a PC. [TechNode reporting]

item.content:encoded:
Unitree Robotics has priced its Shanghai STAR Market IPO at RMB150.80 per share, with 40.45 million shares to be issued. The final strategic-placement list allocated 933,900 shares worth about RMB141 million to Hangzhou DeepSeek AI Basic Technology Research, the developer of DeepSeek.

The allocation is subject to a 36-month lockup. Unitree said strategic investors were selected partly for potential cooperation in large models, embodied intelligence and robotics development. [IT Home, in Chinese]

The company also put its 4,000th battery-swap station and the first batch of fifth-generation stations into operation, expanding support across its Nio, Onvo and firefly brands. Nio said its network now includes 9,166 charging and battery-swap stations, including 1,049 highway […]
item.content:encoded:
Nio said it completed its 120 millionth battery swap at 8:09 a.m. on Aug. 7. The company also put its 4,000th battery-swap station and the first batch of fifth-generation stations into operation, expanding support across its Nio, Onvo and firefly brands.

Nio said its network now includes 9,166 charging and battery-swap stations, including 1,049 highway swap stations. Cumulative electricity delivered through the swaps has reached 6.35 billion kilowatt-hours. [NIO, in Chinese]

item.title: Alibaba Reportedly Plans Revenue-Sharing Terms for Next Qwen Model
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Alibaba is reportedly planning to charge large commercial users of its next open-weight Qwen model by taking a share of the revenue generated from the model’s use. The plan could be introduced as early as next week, but negotiations are still ongoing and the proposed percentage has not been finalized. Alibaba currently charges customers that […]
item.content:encoded:
Alibaba is reportedly planning to charge large commercial users of its next open-weight Qwen model by taking a share of the revenue generated from the model’s use. The plan could be introduced as early as next week, but negotiations are still ongoing and the proposed percentage has not been finalized.

Alibaba currently charges customers that host and use its models through Alibaba Cloud, while customers running most of its open models in their own data centers generally do not pay model fees. The reported plan would extend the company’s monetization model to commercial deployments outside its cloud platform. [IT Home, in Chinese]

item.title: Xpeng Says G9L Testing Covers 26 Countries and 6.74 Million Kilometers
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Xpeng said its G9L SUV has undergone road testing across 26 countries and regions, covering more than 6.74 million kilometers since the project began three years ago. The company said the testing included complex road conditions and extreme environments. The G9L is positioned as a global five-seat flagship SUV and is expected to launch soon, […]
item.content:encoded:
Xpeng said its G9L SUV has undergone road testing across 26 countries and regions, covering more than 6.74 million kilometers since the project began three years ago. The company said the testing included complex road conditions and extreme environments.

The G9L is positioned as a global five-seat flagship SUV and is expected to launch soon, although Xpeng has not announced a specific launch date. The vehicle measures 5.12 meters in length, has a 3.1-meter wheelbase and uses a dual-motor system with a combined peak output of 430 kilowatts. [TechNode reporting]

item.title: StepFun Reportedly Separates Its Model and Agent-Device Businesses
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: StepFun, a Chinese AI company, is reportedly reorganizing around two strategic lines: foundation models and agent devices. Its phone business is being moved into a separate company, while the original entity continues to operate the model business; the plan has not been officially confirmed. StepFun is also reportedly building an overseas commercialization team to sell […]
item.content:encoded:
StepFun, a Chinese AI company, is reportedly reorganizing around two strategic lines: foundation models and agent devices. Its phone business is being moved into a separate company, while the original entity continues to operate the model business; the plan has not been officially confirmed.

StepFun is also reportedly building an overseas commercialization team to sell model APIs, initially focusing on voice models. The company plans to take both its models and phones overseas, with the phones serving as a direct channel for the models. [TechNode reporting]
